craft_notes: Sthāyin: Giving and receiving (audārya); gifts moving both ways. No break→dash hold (shroud held, delay released). Rejected: 'daze' verb for 'dazed' — L3 kept. Read aloud: lands on close.

lines: Ah, ample thy glamour, O Trickster, wherein shrouded —
the dazed delay though thought's hoard on thee be gained.
l4.sanskrit_cite: mahatīyam aho māyā tava māyin yayāvṛtaḥ tvaddhyānanidhilābhe 'pi mugdho lokaḥ ślathāyate

reads_against.argmap: Ah, great is this māyā of yours, O wielder, veiled by which. → Your great māyā veils even treasure-gainers into slackness.
c1_essence: Good discernment sows endless-fruited love; great glamour slackens even treasure-holders.
reads_against.c1_rasa: bhakti with audārya (generosity tasted and returned)

l2.plain_english: Ah, vast is that glamour of yours, O trickster — shrouded in it, the dazed folk turn slack though the hoard of thought on you lie gained.
